newsitem.title: EGYPT: Housing, cement, mills shares top Egypt stocks.
newsitem.headline: Housing, cement, mills shares top Egypt stocks.

text.p: Popular housing firm Heliopolis Housing and Development gained more than 20 percent on Thursday, boosting the Cairo bourse's overall index, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index gained 0.55 points to close at 278.74 while turnover was an above-average 42.84 million pounds ($12.6 million).
"It was a quite day today and with the exception of the cement and housing sectors there were a few natural drops after the recent highs," said Walid el-Khouli of el-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
The bourse hit record highs last week.
Heliopolis Housing and Development was the day's biggest gainer, jumping 55 pounds to close at 300. It accounted for more than 4.30 million pounds of the day's total volume.
Medinet Nasr Housing and Development also saw a boost in its price, rising 23 pounds to close at 288.90.
Helwan Portland Cement topped the day's turnover with trade in shares worth more than 5.90 million pounds. It closed 0.50 higher at 64.

Helwan Cement increased net profits for the financial year 1995/96 to 125.52 million pounds ($36.9 million) from 103.61 million a year earlier. The year ended on June 30. Net profits in the first quarter of 96/97 were 35 million pounds.

The firm, one of Egypt's leading cement manufacturers, had said it was raising dividends for 1995/96 to five pounds from the 4.75 pounds it had promised investors earlier this year. Dividends for 1994/95 were four pounds per share.
Milling firms continued to perform well, with many closing higher. North Cairo Flour Mills ended the day 2.50 pounds higher at 138.50, after trading in more than 1.20 million pounds.

Southern Cairo Flour Mills and Central and Western Cairo Flour Mills both rose 1.50 pounds to close at 69 and 79.50 respectively. Central and Western led turnover in the mills sector, trading in almost 4.0 million pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 425.89 from 433.1 points on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 194.23 from 191.67.
